cs_principles.name: Idempotence
cs_principles.definition: An operation that can be applied multiple times without changing the result beyond the initial application.
cs_principles.verbatim_citation: RFC 7231, Section 4.2.2: 'A request method is considered "idempotent" if the intended effect on the server of multiple identical requests with that method is the same as the effect for a single such request.' URL: https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7231#section-4.2.2
cs_principles.violation: Manual 'run once' steps break idempotence by requiring user intervention.
cs_principles.resolution: All database tables are created on first run via ensure_database() before any query.

cs_principles.name: Automation
cs_principles.definition: Every repeatable action must be scripted; no manual steps.
cs_principles.verbatim_citation: Jose J Melendez, 2026: 'If it can be typed, it MUST be scripted!' (© all rights reserved).
cs_principles.violation: Manual dependency installation and table creation steps.
cs_principles.resolution: ensure_dependencies() auto-installs all tools; ensure_database() creates all tables.

cs_principles.name: Defensive Programming
cs_principles.definition: Designing code to anticipate and handle exceptional conditions.
cs_principles.verbatim_citation: Wikipedia: 'Defensive programming is a form of defensive design intended to ensure the continuing function of a piece of software under unforeseen circumstances.' URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defensive_programming
cs_principles.resolution: Every query is wrapped with table_exists() or OperationalError catch with auto-recovery.
cs_principles.code:
def safe_query(sql, params=()):
    # R070: Wikipedia - Defensive programming - 'Defensive programming is a form of defensive design intended to ensure the continuing function of a piece of software under unforeseen circumstances.' URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defensive_programming
    try:
        with sqlite3.connect(str(DB_PATH), timeout=30, isolation_level='DEFERRED') as conn:
            conn.execute('BEGIN')  # Explicit transaction
            cursor = conn.cursor()
            cursor.execute(sql, params)
            result = cursor.fetchall()
            conn.commit()
            return result
    except sqlite3.OperationalError as e:
        conn.rollback()
        log_verbatim(f'Database error: {e}; recovering...')
        ensure_database()
        with sqlite3.connect(str(DB_PATH), timeout=30, isolation_level='DEFERRED') as conn:
            conn.execute('BEGIN')
            cursor = conn.cursor()
            cursor.execute(sql, params)
            result = cursor.fetchall()
            conn.commit()
            return result
    except Exception as e:
        if 'conn' in locals():
            conn.rollback()
        _log_state('unknown', 'query_fatal', {'sql': sql[:100], 'error': str(e)})
        raise

cs_principles.name: Observability
cs_principles.definition: The ability to collect data about programs' execution, modules' internal states, and the communication between components.
cs_principles.verbatim_citation: Wikipedia: 'In software engineering, observability is the ability to collect data about programs' execution, modules' internal states, and the communication between components.' URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Observability_(software)
cs_principles.violation: No structured logging of state transitions.
cs_principles.resolution: Every state transition emits structured JSON logs with timestamps and correlation IDs.

cs_principles.name: Single Source of Truth
cs_principles.definition: Every piece of knowledge must have a single, unambiguous, authoritative representation.
cs_principles.verbatim_citation: Hunt, A. & Thomas, D. (1999). The Pragmatic Programmer. Addison-Wesley. Chapter 3, p.27: 'Every piece of knowledge must have a single, unambiguous, authoritative representation within a system.' ISBN: 0-201-61622-X.
cs_principles.violation: Patches could be applied multiple times without tracking.
cs_principles.resolution: All patch applications recorded in gd_patch_registry; no duplicate patches.

cs_principles.name: Fail Fast
cs_principles.definition: Detect corruption or errors at the point of occurrence rather than propagating them.
cs_principles.verbatim_citation: Shore, J. (2004). 'Fail Fast.' IEEE Software, 21(5), p.21: 'The Fail Fast principle states that a system should detect failures as early as possible and stop executing.' DOI: 10.1109/MS.2004.1331296.
cs_principles.resolution: _r082_verify() checks sha256 after every write; mismatch triggers immediate error.

cs_principles.name: Separation of Concerns
cs_principles.definition: A design principle for separating a computer program into distinct sections such that each section addresses a separate concern.
cs_principles.verbatim_citation: Dijkstra, E. W. (1974). 'On the role of scientific thought.' In Selected Writings on Computing: A Personal Perspective, pp. 60-66. Springer-Verlag. ISBN: 0-387-90652-5.
cs_principles.violation: Gate script knew about table schema instead of relying on audit script.
cs_principles.resolution: Database layer (ensure_database) handles schema; gate function only checks registry.

cs_principles.resolution: All operations are scripted and produce the same result on repeated runs.

table_defs: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS gd_patch_registry (patch_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, file TEXT, run_id TEXT, content_hash_before TEXT, content_hash_after TEXT, applied_at TEXT, skipped_reason TEXT)

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS auto_heal_actions (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, timestamp TEXT, tool TEXT, action TEXT, file_path TEXT, line_number INTEGER, before_line TEXT, after_line TEXT, success INTEGER DEFAULT 0, error_message TEXT, iteration INTEGER DEFAULT 0)

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pipeline_runs (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, run_id TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, start_time TEXT NOT NULL, end_time TEXT, status TEXT DEFAULT 'running', iteration_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0, errors_found INTEGER DEFAULT 0, errors_fixed INTEGER DEFAULT 0)
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS syntax_errors (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, file_path TEXT NOT NULL, line_number INTEGER, error_text TEXT, code_line TEXT, context TEXT, fixed_ts TEXT)

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS verification_results (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, run_id TEXT, tool_name TEXT, exit_code INTEGER, stdout TEXT, stderr TEXT, errors_found INTEGER DEFAULT 0, verified_at TEXT)
